contracts.detail: SRAM2 only:7ECC bits per32-bit word, single-error correction and double-error detection on reads. Byte/halfword writes involve read-modify-write and may detect double errors. RM warns buffered narrow write commits two AHB cycles after SRAM bus released; no DMA/coherency or timing qualification inferred.

SEDC/DED suppress further respective error detection while set. ALE controls address capture. ICR bits read current ISR flags and writing1 clears them. Capture evidence before clear; no lossless event count implied.

SRAM2 protection covers32 1KiB pages; protection bits andECCNMI cannot clear by ordinary zero writes and RM says globalRAMCFGreset clears them. Software can assertRAMCFGRST viaRCC; whether this is the specified globalreset and its full cross-bank effects remain unqualified. All reset users must share ownership because reset may dropprotection/NMI and resetECC/ALE/IER state. NMI selection suppresses maskable double-errorIRQ regardlessDEIE. No claim software cannot reverse reset-onlycontrols.

Option bytes determine reset ECCE; software disable requires documented key sequence. LL enable sets ECCE+ALE, disable clears both. Existing data/checkbit initialization and option state must be established; no ECC fault injection or destructive action admitted.

Both SRAMs support keyed whole-bank erase. SRAMBUSY persists while ongoing; accesses stall until complete. RM givesN AHB cycles forN32-bit words, not measured latency. Execution code, stack, handlers and DMA must be kept safe from erased bank. API timeout does not cancel erase.

RAMCFG register state retained inStop; powered down inStandby and requires reinitialization. SRAM blocks have optionalStop retention, noStandby retention inTable15. Systemreset/tamper/RDP erase depends exact options and event; full cross-peripheral policy unqualified.

source_derived_SDK_gaps.detail: Exact IS_RAMCFG_WP_INSTANCE acceptsSRAM1 andSRAM2 despite RM115/116 limiting write protection toSRAM2. HAL protection APIs rely on that assertion and can addressSRAM1 WPR1. Do not infer SRAM1 protection from API success.

By-address protection checks alignment only with debug assertions; optional runtime check only validates range. With debug assertions off, SRAM2_BASE+1,size1024 passes optional range check then floors tostart_page0/page_nbr1, protecting one page although requested interval spans two. Independently require page alignment and checked non-overflowing bounds; no hardware observation.

By-address query accepts offset==SRAM_size under <= range with size0; exact SRAM2_END+1 gives page32. Exact32-page build has no WPR2 and reaches1UL<<32, outside32-bit unsigned-long shift range. Independently reject one-past-end address and validate page0..31. Debug docs also say arbitrary in-page addresses are accepted while alignment assertion rejects them. Source-level issue, not compiled/hardware result.

ECC_Disable clears ECC/ALE and attempts DisableIT(ALL), but ECCNMI is reset-only; HAL_OK is not proof NMI routing was released. Preserve ownership/lifecycle requirement. SoftwareRAMCFGRST exists; complete reset effects and bank-wide ownership require qualification before any release strategy.

Enable_IT clears existingECCflags before enabling; prior event evidence can be lost unless captured. IRQ handler calls callback before clear but ignores callback status, unlike NMI handler which clearsDED only on callbackHAL_OK. Default weak callback returnsHAL_ERROR. GetInfo prioritizesDED overSEDC and NONE leavesstatus/address untouched; caller must use type and own snapshots.

MassErase starts before waiting; timeout uses HAL_GetTick and requires tick progression. No cancel or independent content verification on timeout/success; no memory-residency or DMA ownership preflight in helper. NoSRAMBUSYpreflight or independent key-acceptance check. HAL_TIMEOUT also does not establish erase is stillincomplete: actual residency/liveness of tick,stack,code and interrupts caninvalidate timing,including destruction of a timebase in the erasedbank. Actual allocation and resulting behavior unobserved.

Unsigned32-bit range sums can wrap through bothdebug andoptionalruntime checks. EnablePageWRP(start_page=0xffffffff,page_nbr=1) wraps sumto0 and scaledassertsumto0 before a shift by0xffffffff. EnableWRPByAddr(SRAM2_BASE+0x400,size=0xfffffc00) wraps range sumto0; subsequent page iteration reaches shifts>=32. These are conditional source undefined-shift paths, not observed execution. Validate by subtraction/checked arithmetic and nonempty bounded page counts independently.
